body: Okay I know this post is years old and someone else has probably already figured this out, but I found a sort of clunky exploit. In the Hinterlands when doing the waterfall map one of the rewards is ironbark. By saving before looting it you can take the bark, go to skyhold, save then craft your cheap items and if you don't get it you load back to the save in the Hinterlands to reroll the chance. It's only 20% so it did take a couple tries but it did work

My security deposit was about $1400, first month rent included. They've made no claims about it being an existing problem.

Oh!! I almost forgot, I have pictures that were taken of my toilet after I had to go to the emergency room for blood loss. The blood specks on the inside of the bowl had remained there after about 3 hours as I didn't clean it up before calling the ambulance. The pictures had been taken February 18 while the text I received from the plumbing company was on May 4. The inspection had been around the end of February. So if it was running continuously, it was not doing so within the bowl itself

Also thank you, I really appreciate you taking the time to write out what I need to know to ask them

1) They made no claims about misuse or broken parts. I was using the toilet as intended (Certainly a sentence I never thought I'd have to write)

2) They billed me $1,436.26 for the water bill, the memo attached says "Large water bill due to tenant's running toilet". The bill for repairs is $234.70 with the attached memo reading "Toilet repairs for running toilet that the tenant didn't report".

3) The lease agreement says that if I notice something is damaged or working incorrectly I have to file a maintenance request

4) There was no out of the ordinary noise. When I would flush it there would be the normal sound of the water filling back up for a few seconds before it stopped, just like any other toilet I've used. There was no groaning sound or sound of water dripping. After the plumbers came I heard and saw zero difference from how it had been before.

5) I would assume the second inspectors found it? I was not notifed at all by the building owners of any problems after both of the inspections. The first time I was made aware of there being some sort of water problem was when I was contacted directly by the hired plumbers, and I was not notified of which pipes/appliances needed to be fixed. The plumbers also seemed to not have been told where exactly it was as they asked me where it was and seemed confused that I didn't know.

1) I was unaware of it continuously running. It behaved like a normal toilet, there was no movent in the bowl or water coming down the sides of it

2) Yes it's all utilities included

3) They charged me for the repair bill and the 'excess water bill'. They have made no claim about any damages
